sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Iowa Candidates Tackle Cancer Crisis Linked to Farm Pollution
cards.content: Iowa's gubernatorial and Senate races have taken a surprising turn as candidates from both parties focus on addressing the state's cancer crisis, which is linked to farm pollution. The issue has become a political lightning rod amid public health concerns, with nearly $30 million spent on campaign ads mentioning cancer. Republicans and Democrats have staked out positions vowing to take on the issue, with some farmers and environmental advocates criticizing 'Big Ag' practices. The debate has become more heated, with some candidates accusing their opponents of not doing enough to address the crisis. The issue has also caused divisions within the Republican Party, with some MAHA supporters skeptical of the party's commitment to environmental issues.

cards.title: Gunmen Kill At Least 10 in Taraba, Nigeria, amid Attacks
cards.content: Unknown gunmen raided a remote village in Taraba, Nigeria, killing at least 10 people, and possibly up to 50, according to eyewitnesses and a non-governmental organization. The attackers, who arrived on motorcycles, looted shops, set houses ablaze, and fled after a four-hour rampage. The police are searching for other casualties and are accused by Amnesty International of failing to protect rural communities. The Nigerian government is facing criticism for its handling of insecurity, with the country experiencing attacks from armed groups across several regions.

cards.title: Ohio Governor Candidate Vivek Ramaswamy Ends Campaign
cards.content: Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for Ohio governor, has ended his campaign, mirroring President Donald Trump's approach. The controversy arose after an ad featuring the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton, calling Acton a liar and urging voters to reject her. Moderate and independent voters were bothered by the ad, and some said it changed how they view the GOP nominee. While die-hard Republicans who still support Trump remain strongly in Ramaswamy's camp, the controversy may alienate enough voters to hurt the Republican Party's chances in the post-Trump era. The ad's release was met with criticism from some prominent Republicans, including the man Ramaswamy is running to replace, two-term Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. Trump defended the ad, saying it is acceptable for voters to hear and make a decision for themselves.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Females' Burial Sites Suggest Homo Naledi Had Sex-Specific Customs
cards.content: . } The discovery of ancient tooth proteins in South Africa's Dinaledi Chamber has led researchers to believe that the extinct human relative, Homo naledi, might have reserved a burial site exclusively for females. The study, published in Cell, analyzed 23 teeth from at least 20 individuals and found no male proteins, suggesting that the sampled individuals may have all been female. This finding raises the possibility that Homo naledi had a complex custom of sex-specific burial, previously thought unique to modern humans. The discovery also implies that the species might have had a more organized society than previously thought. According to the researchers, tooth enamel can preserve evidence that other skeletal material may lose, making it an ideal carrier of genetic information from deep time. The study helps to explain the long-standing mystery of why Homo naledi lacked significant variation, suggesting that they may have all belonged to one sex. The findings offer rare insights into a culture that has, until now, been difficult to access directly.

cards.title: Scientists Recover Ancient Human DNA from Cave Walls
cards.content: Scientists have made a groundbreaking discovery by recovering ancient human DNA from cave walls, providing a new way to study prehistoric human presence. The researchers, from Spain, Portugal, the UK, China, and Germany, analyzed 24 rock art panels from 11 caves and found five samples that yielded authentic ancient human mitochondrial DNA. Two of these samples came from unpigmented walls and contained no detectable animal DNA, suggesting that humans deposited the DNA directly. The remaining three samples contained both human and animal DNA, indicating an indirect route. The recovered DNA revealed information about some of the people who had been in the caves, including their sex and ancestry. The study suggests that cave walls can hold traces of prehistoric visitors, even when they have no visible signs of human activity. This finding could potentially allow scientists to investigate who used these spaces without disturbing archaeological deposits.

cards.title: AI Takes Over Customer Service, Leaving Humans Dealing with Complex Issues
cards.content: As companies increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to handle customer service, the lives of human customer service representatives are undergoing significant changes. For some, like Kaylee Harris, AI has allowed them to focus more on each customer, while for others, like Shannon, AI-generated notes have led to errors and more work. The automation of routine tasks is meant to free up human agents to handle more complex cases, but some experts warn that this could lead to increased workloads and pressure on employees, potentially causing burnout. As AI takes on more responsibilities, human customer service representatives may be left dealing with a greater share of complicated cases, and the pressure on them comes amid reports of rising workloads across the industry. Experts caution that the push to automate could result in a loss of opportunities for employees to develop the experience needed for more demanding work.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Schizophrenia Linked to Weaker Brain Rhythm
cards.content: A new study published in Science Advances has discovered that changes in brain activity, specifically in a rhythm called beta-band activity, are linked to several symptoms of schizophrenia. Researchers found that patients with schizophrenia showed weaker and slower beta-band activity compared to healthy participants, which was associated with difficulties in processing sensory information, disorganized speech, and severe clinical symptoms. The study suggests that this common disruption in brain activity may be connected to the development of schizophrenia symptoms, including those related to perception, behavior, and speech. The findings could potentially lead to new methods for identifying and supporting individuals at risk of developing psychosis, and even serve as a target for future treatments.

cards.title: Scientists uncover clues to deadly Brazilian virus evolution
cards.content: Scientists have uncovered new clues about the evolution of a rare and deadly Brazilian virus, the Sabiá virus, which has circulated undetected for over a century. Genetic changes allowed the virus to escape existing laboratory tests, leading to the development of an improved detection method. Researchers found that the virus has been circulating in Brazil for approximately 142 years, with likely additional cases going undiagnosed. The study highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in detecting public health risks, particularly in cases where targeted diagnostic tests fail.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: IPCC fails to agree on climate reports timeline
cards.content: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has failed for the sixth consecutive time to agree on a timeline for its Seventh Assessment Cycle reports. The Least Developed Countries are worried that further delays could hinder crucial climate science from informing the second Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement in 2028. Meanwhile, some countries, including India, Saudi Arabia, and Russia, are pushing for the publication of two major reports in 2029 due to concerns over scientific rigor and inclusivity. The IPCC's 65th plenary session in Ethiopia was suspended without an agreement on the publication schedule or budget. This has left the timeline for publishing three Working Group reports unclear, as countries disagree on the pace of the assessment process. The reports cover climate change's physical science, impacts, and mitigation, which are crucial for informing global climate action.

cards.title: Antarctica Turns Green and Red Due to Penguin Droppings Fueling Algae
cards.content: Antarctica, known for its vast expanses of white ice and snow-covered mountains, is unexpectedly turning green and red in some areas. This phenomenon has caught the attention of scientists who are trying to understand the connection to climate change. One factor contributing to the colorful patches is penguin droppings, which provide nutrients to microscopic algae growing on the snow. The scientists suspect that this natural process may accelerate local melting, adding to the effects of a warming climate. The impact of penguin droppings on the melting of Antarctica's snow is still being studied, and the effects are not yet fully understood.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Fender Announces Massive Stadium Tour, Affordable Tickets and No Standing Area Tiers
cards.content: Sam Fender, a 32-year-old musician, announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour for summer 2027, which will visit six cities. Ahead of the tour, Fender responded to a social media post claiming to outline ticket prices, stating he was not happy with the reported costs. He promised to lower the prices, saying they were inflated more than he had intended. Additionally, Fender said he would not split the standing area into front and back tiers, unlike some gigs that have this system. Tickets are due to go on general sale on Friday, with a pre-sale on Wednesday.

cards.title: Nostalgia dominates music streaming, old-school hits lead playlists
cards.content: Music streaming platforms like Spotify and Deezer are facing a paradox. Despite the vast amount of new music being created, people's listening habits have shifted towards nostalgia. In the UK, over 60% of streams are of music released five or more years ago, with classic hits dominating playlists. The same trend is seen in the US, where about 60% of streams are of old-school hits in genres like R&B and Hip-Hop. While some new songs do break out, they often dominate streaming for weeks and months. As a result, aspiring artists may struggle to sustain a career after going viral, as platforms like TikTok are designed for viral moments rather than promoting artists.

cards.title: Rob Brydon plays himself in comedy series The Trip
cards.content: Comedian Rob Brydon, known for his role in Gavin and Stacey, initially doubted the idea of playing a fictionalized version of himself in the comedy series The Trip. However, he enjoyed playing a heightened version of himself, alongside Steve Coogan, and thought it made viewers more curious. The duo stars in the series, directed by Michael Winterbottom, as exaggerated versions of themselves, dining at different restaurants and traveling around the world. In the latest season, titled The Trip to the Northern Lights, they explore Scandinavia, searching for the aurora borealis. Brydon found filming in the region to be breathtaking, despite some cold weather, and enjoyed immersing himself in Scandinavian traditions, including saunas and cold plunges. The release date for the new season has yet to be announced.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Government funds £1 billion for England's social and affordable housing
cards.content: Just over £1 billion will be allocated for social and affordable housing in England, bringing the government's 10-year homes programme funding to over £40 billion. Additionally, mayors and regional leaders are set to receive more powers and funding, with councils allowed to borrow money from the government to invest in housebuilding. The Chancellor, John Healey, will also announce support for small breweries and unveil billions of pounds of new defence spending. The plans aim to give regional leaders more flexibility and authority over investment decisions, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham stating that the goal is to shift power to those who know their communities best. The government will also confirm a new £1.5 billion borrowing facility for mayors from 2028, allowing them to support local priorities such as new homes, high streets, and transport links.

cards.title: Naomi Nomi Revolutionizes Fashion with Quality, Long-Lasting Clothing
cards.content: Naomi Mishkin, the founder of Naomi Nomi, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by producing high-quality, long-lasting clothing at a higher price point. The average customer starts with one shirt and returns for three more within six months, as they realize the value of her products. Mishkin's approach is a departure from the fast fashion industry, which has mastered the art of cutting production costs to the bone. She uses cotton and wool, making her shirts pricier than fast fashion, but lasting longer. Naomi Nomi's success is attributed to the growing backlash against companies that prioritize profit over quality and the environment. The fashion industry has undergone significant changes over the past few decades, with a shift towards planned obsolescence and the use of cheaper materials. However, some consumers are now looking for brands that offer quality, durability, and sustainability, and Naomi Nomi is capitalizing on this trend.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
